subject: Gate 17: the guest driver reported "Windows has not been restarted" although it had been (harness defect, clock skew in the guest)

facts.install_phase_finished: guest clock 2026-10-04T04:15:32Z (SUMMARY.json of gate17-20261004-035322); the host wrote that file at 04:15:38Z
facts.windows_restart: host VBox.log: RUNNING -> RESETTING at 00:31:27 after log start = 2026-10-04T04:18:07Z, guest-initiated (owner: Start > Power > Restart, after "Quit JARVIS completely"); Guest Additions service log opened at host 04:18:51Z
facts.guest_clock_after_boot: the Guest Additions log line written at host 04:18:51Z carries guest time 04:15:55Z: the guest clock was about 2 min 56 s behind the host right after the boot. The same lag is visible after the first boot (guest 03:47:20Z at host 03:47:22Z is in step, but guest 03:48:57Z at host 03:51:53Z after the 03:51 reset). During the previous Windows session the clock caught up to within 6 seconds.
facts.driver_decision: gate-driver-log.jsonl, guest clock 04:24:02Z: "waiting for the Windows restart". Invoke-Gate.ps1 compares the guest's LastBootUpTime with the Install phase's finished_utc; with the guest clock about 3 minutes slow at boot, the boot time reads earlier than 04:15:32Z.
facts.jarvis_after_restart: the owner reports JARVIS opened by itself after sign-in (owner-statements.jsonl; photograph jarvis-after-restart-photo-20261004-042216.jpg)

assessment: False negative of the driver's restart check, not a failure of any gate phase and not a JARVIS defect: no phase was started and nothing was written except the driver log line. The restart itself is proven independently by the host-side VBox.log.
handling: The owner starts the driver once from a Command Prompt inside the VM with the switch that skips only this comparison (E:\gate -NoRestartCheck). Every phase still runs and judges itself; the AfterRestart record carries last_boot as the guest saw it. The switch was written for local rehearsal; its use here is recorded as a deviation. Fix for later tooling: judge the restart by uptime or by a boot identifier, not by wall-clock comparison.
